extracted.intended_audience: growers, handlers, industry stakeholders, and interested persons submitting comments or participating in hearings on USDA marketing orders and FAA NPRMs
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules for participating in Federal Register notice-and-comment proceedings and administrative hearings (USDA marketing orders and FAA NPRMs): how to submit written evidence/comments, applicable deadlines, required contents/copies, and regulatory standards used by agencies for administration (e.g., sales history, allotments, assessments, disposal of excess product).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing evidence submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All persons wishing to submit written material in evidence at the hearing should be prepared to submit four copies of such material at the hearing and should have prepared testimony available for presentation at the hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte communication prohibition for decisional employees
rubrics_metrics.description: From issuance of the hearing notice and until final decision, Department employees involved in the decisional process are prohibited from discussing the merits of the hearing issues on an ex parte basis with any person having an interest in the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibition applies to specified organizational units (Office of the Secretary of Agriculture; Office of the Administrator, AMS; Office of the General Counsel except designated employees assigned to represent the Committee; Fruit and Vegetable Division, AMS). Procedural matters are not subject to the prohibition and may be discussed at any time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment submission requirements (USDA—Irish Potatoes proposed rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments must be received by the specified deadline (February 5, 1990) and submitted in writing to the Docket Clerk, Fruit and Vegetable Division, AMS, at the specified address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three copies of all written material shall be submitted; submissions will be made available for public inspection at the Office of the Docket Clerk during regular business hours. All comments should reference the docket number and the date and page number of the Federal Register issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment submission requirements (FAA NPRM)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments must be received by the specified closing date (no later than February 20, 1990) and be sent in duplicate to the FAA address provided, identifying the Airworthiness Rules Docket number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicable service information may be obtained from manufacturer and examined at FAA offices. All communications received on or before the closing date will be considered; proposals may be changed in light of comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of docket/regulatory identifier in communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications should identify the regulatory docket number and be submitted in the manner specified (duplicate or triplicate as required).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This enables proper filing and consideration (applies across notices — e.g., identify Docket No. and reference the FR date/page).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of comments and docket materials
rubrics_metrics.description: All comments submitted will be available, both before and after the closing date, in the applicable Rules/Docket for examination by interested persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies will make comments available for public inspection at stated docket locations during regular business hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific topics requested for comment (FAA NPRM)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters are specifically invited to comment on the overall regulatory, economic, environmental, and energy aspects of the proposed rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments on these aspects will be considered in the agency's decision-making and regulatory analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement of comment receipt procedure (FAA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters wishing FAA acknowledgement of receipt must submit a self-addressed, stamped postcard with a specified statement; the agency will date/time stamp and return the postcard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a mechanism for commenters to receive confirmation that FAA received their submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency consideration of comments before final determination
rubrics_metrics.description: All written comments timely received will be considered before a final determination is made on the matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency may change proposals in light of comments; a summary report of FAA/public contacts concerned with the substance will be filed in the Rules Docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'handle' (§ 929.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Handle" means (1) to can, freeze, or dehydrate cranberries within the production area or (2) to sell, consign, deliver, or transport (except as a common or contract carrier of cranberries owned by another person) fresh cranberries or in any other way to place fresh cranberries in the current of commerce within the production area or between the production area and any point outside thereof in the United States or Canada.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term explicitly excludes certain activities (see exclusions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Activities excluded from 'handle' (§ 929.10(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'handle' shall not include: (1) sale of nonharvested cranberries; (2) delivery by grower to a handler with packing/processing facilities within production area; (3) transportation from bog to packing/processing facility located within production area; (4) cold storage/freezing of excess cranberries for temporary storage during periods when an annual allotment percentage is in effect prior to disposal pursuant to § 929.59.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'barrel' (§ 929.17)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Barrel" means a quantity of cranberries equivalent to 100 pounds of cranberries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term of office and term limits for committee members (§ 929.21)
rubrics_metrics.description: Term of office for each member and alternate member of the committee shall be two years, beginning August 1 of each even numbered year and ending July 31 two years later. Members serve until successors are selected and qualified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beginning on August 1 of the even numbered year following adoption of amendment, committee members limited to three consecutive terms; alternate members' consecutive terms are not limited. Members serving three consecutive terms may again be eligible after not serving for one full term unless exempted by Secretary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of initial sales history (§ 929.48(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The initial sales history shall be computed by the committee for each grower using the best four out of six years of such grower's sales history, which shall include all commercial sales from the first complete crop year following adoption of this amendment, plus the prior five years of history of commercial sales.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For growers with four years or less of commercial sales history, the initial sales history shall be computed using all available years. The committee, with Secretary approval, may alter the number and identity of years for subsequent computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual recomputation of sales history and formula flexibility (§ 929.48(a)(2)-(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A new sales history shall be computed for each grower after each crop year in the same manner as the initial sales history (using most recent years), and shall use a formula determined by the committee (with Secretary approval) including years during volume regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee may, with Secretary approval, alter number and identity of years used in computing subsequent sales histories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sales history rule for prolonged non-sales due to forces beyond grower's control (§ 929.48(a)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a grower has no commercial sales from established acreage for three consecutive crop years due to forces beyond grower's control, the committee shall compute a level of commercial sales for the fourth year by crediting the grower with the average sales from the preceding three years during which sales occurred; committee may consider all relevant factors regarding lost production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sales history for acreage with no prior history during volume regulation (§ 929.48(a)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: When a grower has no history of sales associated with acreage during a period where a volume regulation exists, the committee shall compute sales history using the greater of: (i) total commercial sales from the acreage, or (ii) state average yield per acre multiplied by the producing acreage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A grower receiving sales history computed under either method shall not be eligible to have deficiencies filled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grower reporting requirement (§ 929.48(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each grower who wishes to market cranberries under the marketing order shall file a report with the committee by January 15 of each crop year indicating total acreage harvested, total commercial cranberry sales in barrels from such acreage, and amount of any new or renovated acreage planted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee may establish rules/regulations for implementing this section with Secretary approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual allotment computation (§ 929.15 and § 929.49(a)-(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A grower's annual allotment for a crop year is the number of barrels determined by multiplying the grower's sales history by the allotment percentage established pursuant to § 929.49. The Secretary shall determine a marketable quantity if limiting the quantity would effectuate declared policy, and the allotment percentage shall equal marketable quantity divided by total growers' sales histories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except as provided in paragraph (f), no handler shall purchase or handle cranberries not within such grower's annual allotment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualification and issuance timeline for annual allotments (§ 929.49(d)-(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Growers must qualify for their allotment by filing with the committee on or before April 15 a form including location of producing acreage, acreage to be harvested, changes in location, and other necessary information (including lease copy). On or before June 1 the committee shall issue to each grower an annual allotment; handlers shall be notified on or before June 1 of the annual allotment that can be handled for each grower whose total crop is delivered to that handler.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a grower delivers to more than one handler, the grower's allotment will be apportioned equitably among handlers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer and allocation of unused allotments (§ 929.49(f)-(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Growers who do not produce cranberries equal to their computed annual allotment may transfer unused allotment to the grower's handler. The handler shall equitably allocate the unused annual allotment to growers with excess cranberries who deliver to such handler; unused annual allotment remaining after transfers shall be transferred to the committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handlers who receive cranberries more than the sum of their growers' annual allotments are 'excess cranberries' pursuant to § 929.59 and must notify the committee. The committee shall equitably distribute unused allotment to all handlers with excess cranberries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment obligation and rate-setting (§ 929.41)
rubrics_metrics.description: Handlers shall pay assessments on all cranberries they acquire as the first handler, as a pro rata share of committee expenses which Secretary finds are reasonable and likely to be incurred, except as provided in § 929.55; payment of assessments may be required throughout the period the part is in effect even if particular provisions are suspended or inoperative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Secretary shall fix the assessment rate to secure funds sufficient to cover expenses and to accumulate/maintain a reserve fund approximately equal to one fiscal period's expenses. Secretary may increase assessment rate at any time and the increase applies to all cranberries acquired during the applicable fiscal period. Committee may accept advance payments and borrow money to provide funds at start of fiscal year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Late payment and interest on unpaid assessments (§ 929.41(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a handler does not pay the assessment within the time prescribed by the committee, the assessment shall be increased by either a late payment charge, or an interest charge, or both, at rates prescribed by the committee with the approval of the Secretary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research, marketing research, and market development funding (§ 929.45)
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee, with Secretary approval, may establish or provide for production research, marketing research, and market development projects designed to assist, improve, or promote the marketing, distribution, consumption, or efficient production of cranberries. The expense of such projects shall be paid from funds collected pursuant to § 929.41 or other funds as approved by the Secretary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The committee may, with Secretary approval, establish rules and regulations necessary for the implementation and operation of this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interhandler transfer reporting and assumption of obligations (§ 929.55)
rubrics_metrics.description: Transfer of cranberries from one handler to another may be made without prior notice to the committee except during a period when a volume regulation has been established. If transfer is between handlers with packing/processing facilities within production area, assessment and withholding obligations shall be assumed by the handler who agrees; if transfer is to handler outside production area, obligation met by handler residing within production area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All handlers shall report such transfers to the committee on a form provided by the committee four times a year or at other times recommended by the committee and approved by the Secretary. Committee may establish rules with Secretary approval for implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creation, identification, inspection, and disposal timetable for excess cranberries (§§ 929.59 and 929.61)
rubrics_metrics.description: Excess cranberries (cranberries received by a handler more than the sum of their growers' annual allotments) shall be identified as the committee specifies, made available for inspection from time received until final disposition, and handled according to committee rules. Prior to January 1 (or other approved date) handlers holding excess must submit a written plan for systematic disposal; prior to March 1 (or other approved date) all excess shall be disposed pursuant to § 929.61.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee may establish rules/regulations for implementation with Secretary approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted outlets for excess cranberries (§ 929.61)
rubrics_metrics.description: Excess cranberries may be disposed only into noncommercial outlets (charitable institutions; USDA-approved R&D projects) or to noncompetitive outlets (nonhuman food use; foreign markets except Canada) that the committee finds, with Secretary approval, meet requirements in paragraph (c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The allowed outlets and criteria are to avoid competition with established markets for regulated cranberries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for diversion of excess cranberries (§ 929.61(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Handlers diverting excess cranberries into noncompetitive or noncommercial outlets must meet the following: (1) Charity: submit institution statement showing quantity received and certifying utilization; (2) R&D: submit report describing project, quantity diverted, and date of disposition; (3) Nonhuman food use: notify committee at least 48 hours prior to disposition; (4) Foreign markets (except Canada): submit copy of on-board bill of lading showing amount loaded for export.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Storage and disposition of withheld excess cranberries subject to committee supervision and accounting control. Committee may establish rules with Secretary approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acreage and sales history transfer rules (§ 929.50 / § 929.48 transfers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Transfers of acreage with established sales history may transfer acreage and associated sales history under conditions: (1) lease agreements must be filed before committee recognition and must include specified information; (2) on total sale, seller and buyer file completed transfer form and buyer has immediate access to sales history computation process; (3) on partial sale/lease, sales history associated with portion transferred shall be transferred and transfer/lease form must include percentage of sales history attributable; (4) no transfer recognized unless transferee and transferor notify committee in writing; (5) in nonregulation year absent sales history use state average yield*acre; (6) during year with volume regulation, transfers without accompanying sales history not recognized until committee receives completed transfer/lease form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee rulemaking authority with Secretary approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Throughout the document, the committee may establish rules and regulations necessary for the implementation and operation of sections, but such rules require the approval of the Secretary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the standard delegative structure: committee drafts operational rules; Secretary must approve for them to take effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reapportionment proposal comment period and consideration (Colorado potatoes)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 30-day comment period is provided to allow interested persons to respond to the reapportionment proposal; all timely received written comments will be considered before a final determination is made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should reference the docket number and the Federal Register citation; three copies requested and will be made available for public inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Flexibility Act (RFA) consideration requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to the RFA, the Administrator has considered the economic impact of the action on small entities and adjusted regulatory actions to fit the scale of affected businesses to avoid undue burden on small entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small agricultural producers defined as annual receipts < $500,000; small agricultural service firms as annual receipts < $3,500,000. Marketing orders are brought about through group action of essentially small entities; majority of handlers and producers may be classified as small entities. Agency must include this consideration in preamble analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAA airworthiness finding for superseding AD
rubrics_metrics.description: The FAA may propose to supersede an existing airworthiness directive if data (e.g., service history) show the originally required periodic action can be eliminated without adversely affecting safety (e.g., factory-assembled wheels not showing cracks vs. field-reworked wheels).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When service data indicate differences in risk by part number or rework history, the AD may remove inspection requirements for some items while retaining them for others; economic impacts (number of affected airplanes, manhours, labor rates) should be estimated and described in the NPRM.
